turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Noah Spencer, thanks for the call. Harbourline IT gives small businesses a full managed IT service for $98 per seat per month, which covers helpdesk, device management, Microsoft 365, backups and security monitoring.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Thanks Jordan. Lumen Lane Retail is ten people if you count casuals. We sell lighting from a Prahran showroom and online. I'm mostly checking prices because our current arrangement is informal.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Informal support is risky for a retailer. If the point-of-sale terminal, Wi-Fi, Xero or email fails, sales stop. A monthly plan means you can call one team and know the fundamentals are being maintained.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: We are comparing you to a break-fix provider who charges by the hour. They quoted a lower rate, and we only call when something is actually wrong.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Break-fix looks cheaper on paper, but it doesn't include prevention. Our agreement includes patching, endpoint protection, backup checks and admin reviews, which is what keeps the hourly emergencies down.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Maybe, but some months we've zero issues. We're not keen to add another subscription while foot traffic is uneven.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: You also need to think about cyber risk. Retailers hold customer details, supplier records and payment systems. If an account is compromised, you want documented controls, not a frantic call to whoever can come out tomorrow.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: I understand, but nobody has asked us for documentation. We don't have a board or a procurement team. It's me, my co-owner and a spreadsheet of expenses.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The onboarding project would clean all that up. For Lumen Lane Retail, it would probably be around $3,800, then the monthly per-seat fee. We'd set MFA, standardise devices and document the environment.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: That's too much for what we need. We were thinking of a few hundred dollars here and there, not a standing agreement.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The issue with a few hundred here and there's that nobody owns the outcome. Managed IT gives you accountability, reporting and a support process that doesn't depend on your co-owner knowing which cable to restart.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: The cable restart isn't worth ten grand a year. We might grow into something like this, but not while the business is this size.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I hear you. Still, the cost of one serious outage can be larger than the annual difference, especially if it happens during a sale or before Christmas.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: That feels a bit hypothetical for us. I wanted to know whether you could beat the hourly provider or offer a small retainer.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: We don't really compete on hourly rates. Harbourline IT's built for proactive managed services, so the value is in coverage rather than being the cheapest emergency contact.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Then I think we will go with the other provider. They fit the way we buy at the moment.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I will send the managed IT brochure in case you want to revisit it later.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Sure, but no need to follow up hard. Thanks for explaining it.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Another thing to consider is that hourly providers aren't usually watching for slow drift. Licences pile up, former staff keep access, routers age out and backups fail quietly until someone finally notices.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: That may be true, but it still feels like buying a large umbrella for a drizzle.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The managed model also gives you reporting. You would see patch status, security alerts, Microsoft 365 settings and recommendations each quarter, instead of only hearing from IT during a fault.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Reports sound nice, but I don't need another report to read.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I get that, but the report is how you know the basics are actually happening. Without it, the cheap option is largely trust and reaction time.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Trust and reaction time are mostly enough for us right now.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: If you change your mind, the brochure explains the minimum standard we recommend for any retailer, even if you don't use us. It might still help you challenge the hourly quote.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: That's useful, but it probably confirms we're shopping in a different category.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I will also include a comparison table between hourly break-fix and managed services. It will show what is included, what is excluded and where responsibility sits, so the decision is clear even if you choose the cheaper path.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: That's fine. A comparison table will probably help my co-owner see why we're saying no, at least for now.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Thanks Noah. Good luck with the showroom.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Thanks, bye.
